notes: Direct HTTP fetch, no blocking. Found a genuine top-level 'New' mega-menu section (page title 'New In | Our Latest Arrivals | Soho Home', H1 'New Arrivals') with real site-defined children: Furniture, Lighting, Rugs & Textiles, Mirrors (product_type facet on /new/home-accessories), Homeware (category facet on /new), and Bathroom, plus an 'All New' parent link (/new). Verified each child is a genuine filtered PLP (not a marketing page) by confirming the 'Selected filters' chips reflect the correct facet values (e.g. product_type=Floor Mirrors,Wall Mirrors for Mirrors; category=diffusers-incense etc. for Homeware) and that category PLPs expose a 'New In' sort option confirming recency-based merchandising. Sum of the 6 children (94+30+30+7+15+12=188) is close to but not an exact match of the parent's 207 - expected, since the mega-menu only surfaces 6 of the site's ~11 top-level categories as New-Arrivals facets (Art, Outdoor, Gifting, Home Fragrance/general home-accessories beyond the 2 facets, etc. have new items rolled into the /new parent but no dedicated /new/<category> child link), so parent is not a strict sum of these 6 - not a data error. Also checked and excluded: homepage 'New arrivals' carousel section (id=new-arrivals) - this is just a product-carousel widget on the homepage, not itself a PLP (it duplicates products already covered by /new); /inspiration/new-collection-aw26 - a marketing/editorial lookbook page for the AW26 season with no product grid, excluded per brief Sec 3 'Collection' rule.
